clue.text: Hero's welcome with flowers red or white

definitions.note: the clue names the plant by its blooms, which come in pinks, reds and white

parts.note: O is a cry of greeting, as Hero might call out on seeing her lover arrive
in Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont each night to Hero, so he is Hero's lover

explanation.surface: A celebrity is greeted with a bouquet of red or white blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' is not a celebrity but the priestess of the legend of Hero and Leander; her greeting to him is 'O, Leander!'
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub is grown for its showy clusters of blossoms, typically pink, red or white.

clue.text: Wildcat 'reverse to the French colonel

indicators.note: reverse tells us the whole string built from the following words is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the
CO, commanding officer, is the colonel in charge of a regiment

explanation.surface: A wild animal backs away from the French colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Robert E. is crazy, mad-but shows spirit

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of the general's surname are jumbled

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
mental is slang for mad

explanation.surface: The Confederate general is said to be crazy, but he shows spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is crazy' turns LEE into ELE before MENTAL is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An elemental is a spirit of one of the four elements, like a sylph or salamander.

clue.text: Man of eminence but without talent

definitions.meaning: read as two words, lacking ability

explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a distinguished figure, and split as 'not able' it means incapable.

clue.text: Lugged a deer in poor shape

indicators.note: poor shape means the letters of a deer are knocked out of form into a new order

explanation.surface: A hunter hauled a sickly deer home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lugged' looks like carried; here it means having lugs, slang for ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Lugs are a slang name for ears, so being lugged is having ears.

clue.text: Its art is involved in the. Channel

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of art is caught up in the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow sea passage joining two larger waters, which is a channel.

clue.text: A victory in the path of Labour?

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the word for a path

parts.note: a trail is a path

explanation.surface: A political party wins a victory on its campaign route.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is hard toil or painful labour, including childbirth.

clue.text: Excuse that I'm neither Tory nor Labour

parts.note: someone of neither main party is a Lib, a Liberal
I, the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone claims political neutrality as a way of getting out of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse reads 'I'm a Lib' as 'a Lib I'; the Liberals were Britain's third party, neither Conservative (Tory) nor Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea of being elsewhere, used as an excuse.

clue.text: Prize for a good servant

definitions.meaning: an invaluable employee is called a gem

explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to cherish it, and a valued helper is called a gem.

clue.text: Such was the majesty of King Philip.

definitions.text: Such was the majesty of King Philip.

parts.words: Such was the majesty of King Philip
parts.note: the kings of Spain, Philip II among them

explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish monarchs bore a papal title naming their Roman faith.

clue.text: German prince with a vote in Durham ?

parts.note: an elector is a person entitled to vote
Durham was a county palatine, ruled by prince-bishops with royal powers, so it was palatine

explanation.surface: A German nobleman somehow has a vote in the English city of Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham, a city and county in north-east England, was for centuries a County Palatine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elector Palatine was one of the princes of the Holy Roman Empire entitled to choose the emperor.

clue.text: Offer competitive price-rise

parts.note: a bidder pushes the price up by offering more than a rival, or more than the thing is worth

explanation.definitionFit: To bid beyond a competitor or beyond value is to raise the price above what was offered.

clue.text: Dragoon Guards as stage villains?

definitions.meaning: the heavy cavalry regiments, such as the Dragoon Guards, were nicknamed by that word
an actor who plays the bad guy is said to play the heavy

explanation.definitionFit: Heavy cavalry regiments were known by the nickname, and theatre slang uses the same word for villains.

clue.text: In some, the real appears insubstantial

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words some, the real

explanation.surface: A philosopher remarks that for some people reality itself seems flimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy and spirit-like, lacking bodily solidity, is insubstantial.

clue.text: Medal so right maybe for high ranks

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A medal might be awarded to people of high rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The titles and domains of earls are high ranks in the peerage.

clue.text: The old railway includes one ship

indicators.note: includes means the railway's letters take the next piece inside them

parts.note: the LNER, London and North Eastern Railway, was a British company merged into British Rail in 1948
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A defunct railway company also owned a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger vessel sailing a regular route is a ship.

clue.text: This parson would not accept a sovereign

definitions.text: This parson would not accept a sovereign

parts.words: This parson would not accept a sovereign
parts.note: after 1688 some clergy refused to swear allegiance to William and Mary as monarchs; 'sovereign' also reads as a gold coin

explanation.definitionFit: Clergy who refused the oath of allegiance were the nonjurors.

clue.text: "Scrannel pipes of —— straw" (Milton)

parts.note: a line of Milton's Lycidas with one word missing, describing feeble shepherds' pipes

explanation.definitionFit: Milton's line in Lycidas reads 'Grate on their scrannel pipes of wretched straw'.

clue.text: What the poor piper constantly did ?

definitions.text: What the poor piper constantly did ?

parts.words: What the poor piper constantly did
parts.note: the piper is a pipe smoker, not a musician, whose pipe keeps going out and has to be lit once more

explanation.definitionFit: A smoker whose tobacco keeps going out puts a match to it again and again.

clue.text: One helps the climber, but a number are boring, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: ten is a number; to drill is to bore holes

explanation.surface: Several dull people are said to help a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant clings with tendrils, which support it.

clue.text: Extorted from the inquisitor's paying guest ?

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective-like word for a noun: rent that is squeezed out of tenants

parts.note: the rack was the Inquisition's instrument of torture
a lodger pays rent

explanation.surface: Money is wrung out of a lodger by a torturer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack-rent is an excessive rent extracted from tenants, money squeezed out unfairly.

clue.text: Employer put up my French abstracts

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a user is one who employs something
mes is French for my

explanation.surface: A boss posts up some French summaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Summaries of documents are abstracts.

clue.text: " Ravelled sleeve " get-ups

indicators.note: ravelled means tangled, so the letters of sleeve are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Macbeth's 'ravell'd sleave of care' recalled as items of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get-ups' is not outfits but risings: a levee was a monarch's reception on getting out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Levees were royal morning receptions held on rising.

clue.text: Irish MP, alone inside, gets clawed.

indicators.note: inside means the word alone goes within the letters for the Irish politician

parts.note: TD, Teachta Dala, is a member of the Irish parliament, the Dail

explanation.surface: An Irish politician on his own is attacked with claws.
explanation.definitionFit: Having talons means having claws, as a bird of prey does.

clue.text: Money's sweet, if vulgar

explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for cash and also for a lollipop or ice lolly.

clue.text: Grass' beyond the river.

parts.note: past means beyond, as in going past the gate
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: There is grass on the far bank of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasture is grassland for grazing animals.

clue.text: Write: to 'the church for money

parts.note: to pen is to write
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone writes to the church asking for funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are coins, small units of money.

clue.text: German league nominally condemned by Voltaire

definitions.text: German league nominally condemned by Voltaire

parts.words: German league nominally condemned by Voltaire
parts.note: Voltaire mocked this German confederation as being neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire: each word of its name was false

explanation.definitionFit: The loose union of German states was famously dismissed by Voltaire on every point of its title.

clue.text: It's uninteresting knowing this method of fishing

parts.note: dry means dull, as in a dry lecture
fly is slang for sharp and knowing

explanation.surface: Someone finds a fishing method dull, though it takes skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Angling with an artificial fly floating on the surface is a style of fly-fishing.

clue.text: Signals from me to the ship take a long time

parts.note: taken as written
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Signals sent from me to a ship take ages to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals are communications sent from one party to another.
